- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

input.description: Find highest fan-in function in internal/
input.prompt:
This is a Go repository at /bench/repo. I need to find which single function or method DECLARED under the internal/ directory has the highest inbound-call count (fan-in) — i.e., the function that is called from the most distinct call sites across the entire repository (internal/, cmd/, server/, store/, proto/, etc., excluding its own declaration and excluding _test.go files unless call sites in tests should also count — count all non-declaration call sites, test and non-test, but note the split).

Steps to do this analysis:
1. Enumerate all function and method declarations under internal/ (files matching internal/**/*.go, excluding _test.go). Use grep for lines starting with `func `.
2. Filter out very generic/common names that are likely interface method implementations rather than true single-definition functions with real fan-in (e.g. String, Error, Validate, Render, New, Init used as method names on many different types) UNLESS you can verify they refer to one specific commonly-called function. Focus especially on:
   - Utility/helper functions in internal/util, internal/base, or similar shared packages
   - Logging helpers, error-wrapping helpers, DB/query helpers, context helpers
   - Small free functions (not methods) since those are unambiguous by name across the whole repo
3. For your top ~10 candidates, run `grep -rn 'funcname(' --include=*.go .` (from /bench/repo) and count occurrences, then manually inspect a sample to confirm they are real call sites (not just the func declaration line, not comments, not unrelated functions with the same name elsewhere).
4. Rank candidates by approximate real call-site count (fan-in), subtracting the declaration itself.
5. Report the winner: the exact symbol name, its receiver type if it's a method, the file path (relative to repo root) where it's declared, and the approximate fan-in count (number of call sites). Also list the next 2-3 runners-up with their counts for context, and briefly explain your counting methodology and any caveats (e.g., name collisions with other packages' functions of the same name that you excluded).

Be rigorous — actually run the greps and verify counts rather than guessing. Keep the final report concise but include the evidence (counts) you found.

```go
func (e *Engine) CompileToStatement(ctx context.Context, filter string, opts RenderOptions) (Statement, error)
```

**Fan-in: 38 call sites total** (7 in production/non-test code, 31 in test code). This is a single unambiguous declaration (verified no other `CompileToStatement` exists anywhere in the repo).

- Test call sites (31): spread across `internal/filter/functions_test.go`, `engine_test.go`, `time_test.go`

2. **`NewEngine`** (free function, `internal/filter/engine.go:24`) — 32 call sites (2 production — inside `DefaultEngine`/`DefaultAttachmentEngine` in the same file — 30 test, concentrated almost entirely in `internal/filter/{engine,functions,time}_test.go`).
3. **`GenUUID`** (free function, `internal/util/util.go:40`) — 28 call sites (7 production across `server/auth/token.go` and several `server/router/api/v1/*.go` files; 21 test, mostly in `server/router/api/v1/test/auth_test.go`).
4. **`DefaultEngine`** (free function, `internal/filter/engine.go:111`) — 7 call sites, notably **all production, zero test** — used by every DB backend (sqlite/postgres/mysql memo & memo_relation files) and two `server/router/api/v1` services.
5. **`AppendConditions`** (free function, `internal/filter/helpers.go:9`) — 6 call sites, also all production, one per DB-dialect memo/attachment query builder.

## Methodology

- Enumerated all `^func ` declarations under `internal/**/*.go` (excluding `_test.go`), 272 total, and separated free functions from methods.
- For candidates, ran `grep -rn '<pattern>(' --include=*.go .` from repo root and manually inspected results to strip out the declaration line itself and confirm every hit was a genuine call (not a comment, doc string, or unrelated symbol).
- Cross-checked for name collisions by grepping `^func <name>(` repo-wide to confirm a single declaration, and, for common short names, by sampling the qualifier before the dot (e.g., `errors.New(`, `grpc.NewClient(`, `sql.Rows.Next()`).

## Caveats / excluded names

- **`New`** had 403 raw hits but is overwhelmingly `errors.New` (263) plus scattered unrelated constructors (`grpc.NewClient`, `uuid.New`, `store.New`, `cache.New`, etc.) — only 2 hits were actually `scheduler.New`. Excluded as a false positive.
- **`Validate`**, **`Compile`**, **`Render`**, **`Send`**, **`Next`**, **`Register`**, **`Start`**, **`Stop`**, **`Field`** are common interface-style method names implemented/called on many unrelated types across the repo (e.g. `.Next()` is dominated by `database/sql`'s `rows.Next()`, `.Register`/`.Start` mostly only appear in doc-comment examples for `internal/scheduler`). These were excluded from ranking since their raw grep counts don't reflect a single function's real fan-in.
- Counting rule: "call site" = any non-declaration textual occurrence of `funcname(`/`.MethodName(` matching the unique declaration, both production and test code, per the task's instructions — hence the test-heavy skew noted for `CompileToStatement`, `NewEngine`, and `GenUUID`.</result>
